paragraphs.text: From June to December 2022, 61 organisations in the United Kingdom took part in a trial involving around 2,900 employees. Participants committed to reducing working time by 20% while keeping pay unchanged. Researchers examined whether a shorter week could protect employees' well-being without undermining business performance. The results were reported in February 2023.

Preparation lasted two months and included workshops, coaching and support from other participants. Employers did not all adopt the same timetable. Some used a common day off; others staggered employees' days off. The report describes several arrangements, including annualised and conditional schedules. Its central requirement was unchanged pay alongside a meaningful reduction in working time. Each organisation adapted the policy to its own operations.

Employers also looked for ways to streamline work. They shortened meetings, made agendas clearer and introduced periods when employees could concentrate without interruptions. Some changed email practices or prepared task lists to improve handovers. These changes were intended to help organisations meet their targets within fewer working hours. The trial therefore involved reorganising work, as well as changing the weekly schedule.

The report compared workers' experiences before and after the trial. At the end, 71% reported lower burnout and 39% reported less stress. These figures describe employees' reported experiences, rather than a guarantee that everyone benefited. Employee retention was another business consideration: the report recorded fewer staff departures. Of the 61 participating companies, 56 planned to continue the shorter week, and 18 confirmed a permanent change.

Revenue figures need careful interpretation. Cambridge reported an average increase of 1.4% during the trial for the 23 organisations able to provide revenue data. That figure does not describe all 61 participants. Interviews also revealed concerns: some employees worried about more intense workloads, while others felt that less informal conversation could reduce opportunities for new ideas.

The evidence came from company records, employee surveys and interviews collected during the pilot, with measurement points at its beginning, middle and end. These different sources allowed researchers to examine both organisational outcomes and individual experiences. The varied schedules are also significant: a four-day week was not one uniform policy applied in exactly the same way to every participating workplace.

vocabulary.definition: keeping existing employees in an organisation
vocabulary.context: Employee retention was another business consideration: the report recorded fewer staff departures.
vocabulary.example: The company reviewed employee retention after introducing flexible schedules.
vocabulary.testedSense: 従業員が組織に在籍し続けること

ja.explanation: ここでは従業員が辞めずに在籍し続けること。採用・配置・昇進とは異なる。

en.explanation: retentionは既存の従業員を組織にとどめること。新規採用・昇進・研修ではない。

combinations.nuanceJa: 在籍している人材が辞めずに働き続けること。新規採用とは分ける。
combinations.example: Employee retention improved after the team introduced regular mentoring.

combinations.nuanceJa: 人材が残りやすくなる方向への変化を表す。
combinations.example: The manager reviewed whether flexible shifts could improve retention.

combinations.nuanceJa: 定着を測定する割合。対象期間と人数の定義が必要。
combinations.example: We measured the retention rate over the first twelve months.

vocabulary.definition: make a process simpler and more efficient
vocabulary.context: Employers also looked for ways to streamline work.
vocabulary.example: We streamlined the approval process by removing unnecessary steps.
vocabulary.testedSense: 不要な複雑さを減らして業務を効率よくする

ja.explanation: streamlineは工程を簡素化して効率を高めること。外注・権限の分散・自動化そのものを意味しない。

choices: transfer work to an outside supplier
en.explanation: 業務を簡素化し効率を高める意味。外注化・分権化・自動化は別の概念。

combinations.nuanceJa: 工程の重複や無駄を減らす。自動化するとは限らない。
combinations.example: The team streamlined the process by combining two approval steps.

combinations.meaningJa: 業務運営を効率化する
combinations.nuanceJa: 個別工程より広い日常業務全体を対象にする。
combinations.example: A shared booking system helped the clinic streamline operations.

combinations.meaningJa: 連絡の流れを簡素化する
combinations.nuanceJa: 連絡経路や手順を整理する。会話を減らすこと自体ではない。
combinations.example: We streamlined communication by choosing one channel for urgent requests.

vocabulary.definition: make something weaker or less effective
vocabulary.context: Researchers examined whether a shorter week could protect employees' well-being without undermining business performance.
vocabulary.example: Repeated changes to the deadline undermined confidence in the plan.

ja.explanation: ここでは業績を弱めたり悪化させたりする意味。調整・評価・維持ではない。

choices: keep something in its current condition
make something weaker or less effective
change something to suit new conditions
en.explanation: ここでは業績を弱めたり悪化させたりする意味。調整・評価・維持ではない。

combinations.nuanceJa: confidenceの対象はinで続ける。信頼を弱める。
combinations.example: Unexplained delays undermined confidence in the delivery plan.

combinations.nuanceJa: 努力の効果を弱める。努力そのものがなくなるとは限らない。
combinations.example: Conflicting instructions undermined efforts to reduce errors.

combinations.nuanceJa: 人や組織の指示が受け入れられる力を弱める。
combinations.example: Publicly reversing every decision undermined the supervisor's authority.

vocabulary.definition: arrange events to happen at different times
vocabulary.context: Some used a common day off; others staggered employees' days off.
vocabulary.example: We staggered lunch breaks to keep the reception desk staffed.

ja.explanation: 休日や開始時刻を同時にせず分散させる意味。単なる順番の変更・延長・回数削減とは異なる。

choices: arrange events in a different sequence
make events last for a longer period
arrange events at different start times
reduce the number of scheduled events
en.explanation: 休日や開始時刻を同時にせず分散させる意味。単なる順番の変更・延長・回数削減とは異なる。

combinations.nuanceJa: 全員が同時に開始しないようにする。
combinations.example: The organiser staggered start times to avoid a queue at the entrance.

combinations.meaningJa: 昼休憩の時間をずらす
combinations.nuanceJa: 休憩を分散し、人員配置を維持する。
combinations.example: We stagger lunch breaks so that someone can answer customer calls.

combinations.meaningJa: 支払い時期を分散する
combinations.nuanceJa: 支払いを別々の時期に配置する。単なる期日の延期とは異なる。
combinations.example: The buyer asked to stagger payments across three months.

vocabulary.definition: the same across a group or range
vocabulary.context: The varied schedules are also significant: a four-day week was not one uniform policy applied in exactly the same way to every participating workplace.
vocabulary.example: The branches use a uniform process for handling refund requests.

ja.explanation: ここでは全職場で同じように適用される意味。制服という名詞ではなく、形容詞の一律の。

choices: temporary until a final decision is made
the same across all members of a group
requiring close obedience to every rule
left to the choice of each participant
en.explanation: ここでは全職場で同じように適用される意味。制服という名詞ではなく、形容詞の一律の。

combinations.nuanceJa: 対象ごとに別方針を使わず、共通の方針を適用する。
combinations.example: The company adopted a uniform policy for refund requests.

combinations.nuanceJa: 複数の場所や対象に同じ基準を使う。厳しさとは別。
combinations.example: Uniform standards made it easier to compare inspection results.

combinations.nuanceJa: 何の範囲で同じなのかをacrossで示す。
combinations.example: The reporting format is uniform across all regional offices.

comprehension.question: Which condition was central to the trial?
choices: Employees kept their pay while working less.
Employees accepted less pay for fewer hours.
Employees worked longer days for extra pay.
Employees chose any schedule without limits.
comprehension.explanationJa: P1の賃金維持と労働時間削減へのコミット、P2の unchanged pay alongside a meaningful reduction が根拠。単に勤務日を詰める制度ではない。

comprehension.question: Why should a reader avoid treating the 1.4% increase as a result for all participants?
choices: The revenue data cover only part of the trial.
The figure measures only changes in staff pay.
The interview data replace all revenue records.
The participating firms all used one schedule.
comprehension.explanationJa: P5は売上データを提供したのが23組織で、試行参加は61組織と述べる。したがって、この平均から残りの組織を含む全参加企業の結果までは判断できない。「1.4%は誤り」や「未提供企業は悪化した」とも推論できない。

comprehension.question: Which concern did the Cambridge interviews identify?
choices: Every firm lost the ability to meet its targets.
Less informal talk might limit chances for ideas.
All workers received less pay during the trial.
The trial had no data about company revenue.
comprehension.explanationJa: P5で一部の従業員は非公式な会話の減少が新しいアイデアの機会を減らし得ると感じている。全員の不利益や全社の目標未達とは述べていない。

opinion.prompt: Would a shorter working week suit a workplace you know? Explain one possible benefit, one possible difficulty, and one result you would measure.

review.notes: P7削除。本文内の5語を選定し直した。使い方はすべて未確認。本文と設問の再確認待ち。
